correctness.rationale: The exact Fourier-Bessel transform, obtained by differentiating the Laplace-Bessel transform for Re z>0, has at radial frequency zero the numerator 3-6t-t² over (1+t)^3. Thus t>2sqrt(3)-3 is excluded. For all t≤2sqrt(3)-3, every radial frequency is controlled by a six-degree polynomial in u=tan(phi)/sqrt(t). A validated exact seven-coefficient Bernstein basis expansion has nonnegative coefficients, with only the last possibly vanishing at the threshold and only at u=1 (zero frequency). Positive density on all nonzero radii gives strict positive definiteness for all distinct finite sites. CHECK.py verifies algebra and numerical cross-checks but the analytic Bernstein argument supplies the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The Euclidean dimension-three Matérn-cosine restriction bound omega/a≤1/sqrt(5) is strictly more restrictive and cannot imply the planar value sqrt(2sqrt(3)-3). Published unweighted damped-cosine bounds concern a different radial function, and Gneiting (2011) does not classify cosine-modulated Matérn kernels. Hu et al. (2013) construct oscillating Gaussian random fields from a different reciprocal-quartic spectral family. Searches of the published-results index and mathematical literature showed no statement or stronger result implying this planar threshold, but this is not an exhaustive originality certificate.

value.rationale: This gives the exact planar oscillation interval of a natural smoothness-3/2 Matérn covariance profile combined with radial oscillation. The sharp threshold cannot be inferred from 1D or 3D bounds: the new admissible planar range beyond the 3D restriction is nontrivial. Its Bernstein certificate gives a structural all-frequency positivity mechanism and the origin-frequency obstruction supplies sharp failure. Applications to valid/invalid spatial covariance parameterization and strict interpolation make the exact fact useful.
